entities.name: Adolescent PCOS
observations: In adolescents with obesity and clinical features of PCOS, screening for impaired glucose tolerance or type 2 diabetes is indicated.
A 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test is the most sensitive screening approach when risk is high, including obesity and acanthosis nigricans.

entities.name: Insulin resistance
observations: Acanthosis nigricans and severe obesity are clinical markers of insulin resistance and increased risk for dysglycemia.

entities.name: 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test
observations: The 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test detects impaired glucose tolerance that may be missed by fasting glucose or hemoglobin A1c, and is preferred for high-risk adolescents with PCOS features.

entities.name: Secondary overtriage
observations: Potentially avoidable interfacility transfer to a higher-level trauma center, commonly defined retrospectively by low injury severity, no operation or interventional procedure, no ICU need, survival, and rapid discharge; definitions are heterogeneous.
Reported rates range from 11.6% in transferred renal trauma to 43% in a rural Level I trauma-center activation cohort, but estimates are not directly comparable.
Main demonstrated harms are avoidable transport, duplicated diagnostics, receiving-center capacity use, family burden, and cost; causal excess mortality has not been established.
Rural hospitals face capability and access constraints, so retrospective overtriage classification may overstate inappropriate transfer.
Tele-trauma, specialist consultation, diagnosis-specific protocols, local observation pathways, and balanced audit of undertriage are promising but incompletely validated.
